primitives.name: Completion Probability Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Completion Probability / CPOE - **NGS definition:** probability of a pass being completed under given conditions (nfl.com, Sep 21 2018).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: [{'symbol': 'P_{comp}', 'unit': 'dimensionless', 'definition': 'Probability of pass completion'}, {'symbol': '\\mathbf{x}_{pass}', 'unit': 'mixed', 'definition': 'Vector of 10+ in-play features including pressure, throw depth, separation, sideline proximity'}]
primitives.assumptions: Independent feature contributions, stationary feature distributions across seasons, and balanced class priors in training data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where pressure exceeds 75% threshold triggers rapid decline in conditional completion probability.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a Bayesian logistic regression with elastic net regularization, equivalent to the published XGBoost ensemble.
layer2.telemetry: Observed pass completion rates conditional on pressure score and throw characteristics

primitives.name: Expected Rushing Value Calculation
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Public model description:** XGBoost ML model hosted on Amazon SageMaker (amazon.science, Feb 2026 — "blended the factors that shape a throw's outcome, from quarterback pressure to throw depth, receiver separation, and sideline proximity").
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: [{'symbol': 'xRY', 'unit': 'yards', 'definition': 'Expected rushing yards'}, {'symbol': '\\Omega', 'unit': 'none', 'definition': 'Set of possible rushing outcomes'}, {'symbol': '\\mathbf{z}_0', 'unit': 'none', 'definition': 'Initial feature vector at handoff'}]
primitives.assumptions: Spatial homogeneity of feature effects, temporal independence of outcome probabilities, and convex loss landscape for CRPS minimization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where defenders intercept the ball carrier before reaching the first down marker, causing negative xRY values.

layer2.mapping: Equivalence to a convolutional neural network operating on a grid representation of player displacements, sharing weight matrices across spatial locations.
layer2.telemetry: Actual rushing yards observed in game logs, used as ground truth for CRPS computation

primitives.name: Pressure Score Quantification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Public proxies: NFL Big Data Bowl Kaggle datasets (annual tracking releases), nflverse (nflreadr) play-level aggregates.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: [{'symbol': 'PS', 'unit': 'binary', 'definition': 'Pressure indicator variable'}, {'symbol': 'P_{press}', 'unit': 'dimensionless', 'definition': 'Probability that a defender applies pressure within 2.5 seconds'}]
primitives.assumptions: Bernoulli trials for pressure events, constant threshold across all defensive fronts, and independence between pressure occurrences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where multiple defenders converge on the quarterback simultaneously, increasing joint pressure probability beyond 0.9.

layer2.mapping: Thresholding a multi-class classification output from the XGBoost model, mapping continuous scores to binary high-pressure indicators.
layer2.telemetry: Observed instances of sacks, hits, and hurries recorded in the Next Gen Stats database

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is translating noisy, high-dimensional spatiotemporal tracking data into interpretable game-theoretic quantities. We address this by constructing a universal lens that embeds all players into a shared latent space, respecting physical constraints such as bounded velocity and acceleration. Dualities emerge naturally: optimal passing routes correspond to Nash equilibria in a zero-sum game between offense and defense, while run-blocking assignments can be seen as Stackelberg leader-follower dynamics. Failure modes include adversarial examples where defenders exploit model uncertainty, requiring robust optimization techniques. The conformal inference layer provides worst-case coverage guarantees, mitigating catastrophic miscalibration.

Weighted conformal calibration further ensures distribution-free finite-sample coverage even under covariate shift between historical training splits and live operational weeks. Crucially, zero-leakage chronological causality demands that every parameter, variance weight, and situational adjustment strictly precede the target event horizon, preventing forward leakage or post-hoc optimization bias.
